findings.title: Freeze arithmetic overflow and underflow behavior for finite positive prices
findings.trigger: Admitted P0 near the smallest positive binary64 and P1=1.0 are both finite/positive, but the Float64 quotient cannot be finite. Very close/subnormal endpoints can also underflow differences or lose precision.
findings.consequence: Input-only finiteness does not define whether mature label values may be infinity, rejected, or represented differently; independent implementations can disagree and canonical finite-result serialization can fail.
findings.requested_change: Before Ready specify the Float64 operation order, finite-result/overflow policy and tolerance domain, then add independent extreme-range fixtures. Treat unsupported output range as a typed error or explicitly governed status; never serialize a mature nonfinite return.

findings.title: Give pending and incomplete states a total precedence
findings.trigger: t1<=C, exact endpoint absent, and basis known-at unknown or later than K simultaneously meet the pending and incomplete definitions. Mixed false and unavailable scanner predicates likewise have no stated entity-state precedence at line17.
findings.consequence: The same valid immutable request can receive different status/reason outputs depending on check order, violating complete deterministic parity and maturity semantics.
findings.requested_change: Before Ready freeze a truth table for endpoint presence, horizon, endpoint/basis admission and invalid inputs, and a scanner mixed-predicate table. Include independent crossed-condition fixtures and preserve all required reason dispositions.
